scripts.//build: vite build only fills _app/dist. Nothing is published until `publish` syncs it out to the repo root, which is where GitHub Pages serves from.
scripts.//publish: Copies dist/ to the repo-root paths this project owns (index.html, 404.html, assets/, and the section shells such as profile/index.html) and then ASSERTS the whole URL contract. It refuses to touch terms/, privacy/, iptv, data/ or device/agent/ — those are published directly by the browser console and must never depend on a build.
scripts.//serve:site: Serves the REPO ROOT, which is exactly what GitHub Pages serves: the published build output plus the static contract it must not touch. `npm run preview` only serves _app/dist, so it cannot show /terms/{slug}/ at all.
scripts.//check:live: Byte-compares every path that must never change against the deployed site. Needs no server. This is the pre-push gate for the app-store URLs.
scripts.//cv: Prints the /profile/cv page to src/features/profile/assets/cv.pdf with headless Chrome — the file the profile's DOWNLOAD button serves. Run it after editing the CV, then build and publish.
scripts.//helper:build: The Device Lab helper is TypeScript in helper/src. This bundles it with rolldown into ONE readable file, ../device/agent/device-bridge.mjs, the file testers download and run with plain Node. Committed by hand, like the rest of device/agent/. `-- --check` only reports whether the committed file is stale.
scripts.//helper:fake: The BUILT helper (../device/agent/device-bridge.mjs) on 127.0.0.1:8787 with the helper suite's fake phones, fake usbmuxd and fake adb server, for Device Lab UI work without phones: run it next to `npm run dev`, open the link it prints, and type `help` for the commands (plug, trust, lock, devmode, xcode, adb, simulators). Nothing on this Mac is run.
scripts.//: Composite scripts below are the single source of truth for .vscode/tasks.json. Task definitions stay thin wrappers so the two cannot drift.
scripts.//verify: typecheck is separate from build on purpose: `vite build` does NOT type-check, so a green build proves nothing about types. The helper has its own typecheck, tests and a staleness check of the committed device-bridge.mjs.
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:helper && npm run lint && npm test && npm run test:helper && node helper/build.mjs --check && npm run build
scripts.deploy: npm run verify && npm run publish
